title: The Widower True Story: Where Is Thomas Randolph Now?

lines.say: In May 2008, a man in Las Vegas called 911.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC HOUSE, NOT THE REAL HOME

lines.say: His wife had been shot, he said, by a masked intruder.
And he said something else. He'd wrestled the gun away from the man, and shot him.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC HOUSE, NOT THE REAL HOME

lines.say: The man he shot wasn't a stranger.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC HOUSE, NOT THE REAL HOME

lines.say: He was Michael Miller, a thirty-eight-year-old handyman the caller knew.
The caller was Thomas Randolph. And Sharon, his sixth wife, was dead.
Prosecutors would later tell a jury a very different story. They alleged Randolph had hired Miller to kill Sharon, then shot Miller to silence a witness.
Randolph says he's innocent.
He has now stood trial for murder three times.
One jury acquitted him. Two juries convicted him.
And the first of those convictions, with its two death sentences, was thrown out, because the jury had heard about a death he'd already been acquitted of.
To understand how that happened, we have to go back to Utah, more than twenty years before that 911 call.
This is the true story behind Netflix's The Widower, and where Thomas Randolph is now.
Thomas Randolph has been married six times.
His first marriage lasted from 1975 to 1983. That wife is still alive, and years later, she testified against him.

rows.text: She is alive · Testified at his trial

lines.say: In 1983 he married Becky Gault. According to reports, it was the same day his divorce came through.

rows.text: per the Las Vegas Review-Journal, via Oxygen

lines.say: After Becky, there were four more marriages.

rows.text: Outlets list wives three to five

lines.say: Four of his six wives have died. But those deaths were very different, and the law has treated them very differently.

shots.label: of his wives have died
shots.note: Causes and legal outcomes differ; they follow.

lines.say: One died in 2004, after heart surgery. Another died of cancer. He was never charged over either death.

shots.title: Two deaths from medical causes
items: Francis Randolph · Died 2004, after heart surgery

lines.say: One, in Utah, led to a murder trial. And one, in Las Vegas, led to the sentence he's serving now.
Utah. November 1986.
Becky Gault, Randolph's second wife, died at home from a gunshot wound.
At first, her death was ruled a suicide.
Then a former friend and co-worker, Eric Tarantino, went to the authorities. He told them Randolph had talked about having Becky killed, for the insurance money.
Randolph was charged with her murder.
And while he sat in jail waiting for trial, according to news reports, he offered a cellmate cash, and the title to a car, to kill Tarantino.

rows.text: Offered: cash and a car title,

lines.say: The cellmate was an undercover police officer.
Randolph pleaded guilty to felony witness tampering.
The murder charge was a different story. At trial in 1989, his lawyers argued that Becky had taken her own life.
And the jury acquitted him.
Remember that acquittal. Three decades later, in a courtroom in Las Vegas, it would matter again.
By 2008, Randolph was living in Las Vegas with his sixth wife, Sharon.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC HOUSE, NOT THE REAL HOME

lines.say: Prosecutors would later say he'd taken out life insurance on Sharon in the two years before she died, and stood to collect more than $300,000.

shots.label: Life insurance on Sharon, prosecutors said
shots.note: Reported figures range up to about $400,000

lines.say: Investigators went through the phone records, too. They counted nearly 300 calls between Randolph and Miller in the months before the shootings. Most, they said, were made by Randolph.
Randolph told police Miller was wearing a mask when he shot him.
But police said Miller had been shot in the forehead. And the ski mask was found on the garage floor, with no blood on it, and no bullet holes.
Then there was the 911 call itself.
Prosecutors said the dispatcher had to ask Randolph several times to give Sharon CPR.

head: PROSECUTION · THE 911 CALL
DEFENCE · THE 911 CALL
body: The only one who helped her

lines.say: His defence argued the call showed something else: a man screaming and crying over his wife, and the only person who tried to help her.
Detectives also filmed Randolph walking them through the house. On that video, he acts out the shootings and, one station reported, mimics the sound of the gunfire.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC HOUSE, NOT THE REAL HOME

lines.say: Jurors at both of his trials would watch it.
His defence argued there was no physical evidence of any plot, and that Miller acted alone, in a burglary that went wrong.

head: THE PROSECUTION
THE DEFENCE
body: No physical evidence of a plot

lines.say: Eight months after the shootings, in January 2009, police arrested Randolph at his parents' home in Clearfield, Utah. He was fifty-three.

depicts.act: being arrested at his parents' home

lines.say: He was charged with conspiracy to commit murder, and with murder.
And then, he waited. It would be almost nine years before his first trial.
In 2017, the case finally went to trial in Las Vegas.
And this time, the jury heard about Utah: Becky's death, and witnesses who said Randolph had tried to arrange her killing.
Before that evidence could be used, the judge held a hearing. The State called just one witness: the prosecutor from Randolph's Utah murder trial.
The jury heard all of it, even though Randolph had been acquitted of Becky's murder.
Two of his former wives testified, too.
On the 28th of June, 2017, the jury found Randolph guilty of conspiracy, and of two counts of first-degree murder.
A week later, the same jury, eight women and four men, sentenced him to death, twice. One sentence for each victim.
He appealed. And on the 10th of December, 2020, the Nevada Supreme Court threw out the convictions and both death sentences, and ordered a new trial.
The reason was Utah. The court said that evidence should never have been admitted, because the risk of unfair prejudice substantially outweighed its value.
It found the State's proof of those old allegations rested on a single witness. And it pointed out that Randolph had been acquitted.

shots.title: Nevada Supreme Court · 2020
items: The proof rested on one witness

lines.say: The ruling didn't mean he was innocent. It meant he'd be tried again.
Two months later, Dateline NBC aired a three-part series about the case. It was called The Widower.
The retrial began in August 2023.
This time, prosecutors were largely limited to the deaths of Sharon and Michael Miller. And they didn't seek the death penalty.
Defence attorney Josh Tomsheck told the jury there was no physical evidence of a plot, and that Randolph was the only person who tried to help Sharon that night.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC LAWYER, NOT A LIKENESS

lines.say: The jury deliberated for more than four hours. Then it found Randolph guilty of conspiracy to commit murder, and of two counts of murder with a deadly weapon.
In April 2024, Judge Tierra Jones sentenced him to sixty years to life in prison.
At his sentencing, Randolph spoke.
"I didn't kill Sharon," he said. "I have nothing to do with this."

shots.text: I didn't kill Sharon. I have nothing to do with this.

lines.say: He appealed again. He argued that years of delay had violated his right to a speedy trial, and that what he told detectives on that walkthrough video wasn't voluntary.
On the 31st of August, 2026, the Nevada Supreme Court rejected every one of his arguments, and upheld the convictions.
The nine years before his first trial, it said, didn't violate his rights. The nineteen-month wait before the retrial was long enough to be presumed prejudicial, but the State wasn't to blame.
He'd also said he was in pain, and on medication, when he spoke to detectives. Two detectives testified otherwise, and the court let his statements stand.
Today, Thomas Randolph is in his seventies, serving his sentence at Lovelock Correctional Center in Nevada.
He says he is innocent.
One journalist had been there almost from the start. Dateline producer Dan Slepian was embedded with Las Vegas police in 2008, and followed the case for years.
On the 30th of September, 2026, Netflix released The Widower: 'Til Death Do Us Part, directed by Chris Smith.

rows.text: The Widower: 'Til Death Do Us Part

lines.say: It follows Slepian, and Las Vegas police detective Dean O'Kelley.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC DETECTIVE, NOT A LIKENESS

lines.say: In its first week, it drew 11.6 million views, and was reported as Netflix's number-two English-language film worldwide.
So, here's where the record stands.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC HOUSE, NOT THE REAL HOME

lines.say: In Utah, a jury acquitted Randolph of murder in Becky Gault's death. He pleaded guilty to witness tampering.
No charge was ever brought over the deaths of two of his other wives.
In Las Vegas, two juries convicted him of murdering Sharon and Michael Miller. The first verdict was thrown out. The second has been upheld.
Thomas Randolph says he didn't kill Sharon. Two juries said that he did.
